_readme: Mode-A recall eval for the LLM key-metrics preselect (directives/key_metrics_picker.md). Score = RECALL of `expected_metrics` (the must-have key metrics a fundamental analyst would put on the dashboard); a case passes at recall >= 0.5. Each case carries its own `vocabulary` (the closed token set the production call picks from) so the eval exercises the real closed-vocabulary discipline; every expected/also_valid token must be IN the vocabulary. `also_valid` are correct-but-not-required picks counted only in precision. business_description is answer-neutral (describes the business model, never names a metric) so it can't leak the expected set. The vocabulary deliberately mixes the load-bearing operating KPIs with generic accounting-line distractors (total assets, COGS, SG&A) the generator should rank below them. Re-run: python execution/run_llm_evals.py --purpose key_metrics --min-score 0.6

cases.name: Nu Holdings
cases.business_description: A branchless, app-only digital financial-services platform serving retail consumers across Latin America. Acquires customers at near-zero marginal cost through a mobile app, monetizes via interchange, a fast-growing unsecured-lending book, and net interest income on low-cost deposits. The thesis is consumer-banking disruption: cheap funding, expanding monetization per customer, and credit underwriting that stays disciplined as the loan book scales.

cases.name: ServiceNow
cases.business_description: An enterprise software-as-a-service company selling a cloud workflow and automation suite to large organizations on a recurring subscription basis. Lands with IT service management and expands across the enterprise; growth is seat- and module-expansion driven with strong operating leverage. The thesis rides durable recurring revenue, customers spending more over time, and a large contracted backlog converting to revenue.

cases.name: MercadoLibre
cases.business_description: A Latin American online marketplace bundled with a payments and digital-financial-services arm. Monetizes through marketplace take rate, advertising, logistics, and payment processing plus a growing consumer-credit book. The thesis is an e-commerce-plus-fintech flywheel in emerging markets: more buyers and sellers drive more transactions, which feed the payments and credit business.

cases.name: Uber Technologies
cases.business_description: A global on-demand marketplace matching consumers with drivers and couriers for ride-hailing and delivery, plus a freight brokerage. Monetizes by taking a percentage of each transaction it facilitates. The thesis is network-effect liquidity: more active platform users drive more bookings, improving take economics and pushing the platform to sustained cash generation.

cases.name: Meta Platforms
cases.business_description: A social-media and messaging company whose family of apps reaches billions of people, monetized almost entirely through digital advertising sold against user attention. The thesis is engagement times monetization: keep people active across the apps and raise the value extracted from each one, while managing the cost of the content-recommendation and AI infrastructure.

cases.name: Veeva Systems
cases.business_description: A vertical software-as-a-service provider of cloud applications and data products built specifically for the life-sciences industry. Sells recurring subscriptions to pharma and biotech for commercial and R&D workflows, expanding from a CRM beachhead into a broad product suite. The thesis is durable recurring revenue, land-and-expand within a sticky regulated customer base, and high software margins.
